ledger.claim: The driver's own trace shows he held position inside the pickup geofence for only 144 seconds, from 13:31:56 to 13:34:20, before cancelling at 13:34:24. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec), so the effective in-geofence dwell falls 36 seconds short of the minimum. Under POL-NS-06 the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages.

The shortfall is confirmed by the derived arrival block itself: longest_run_sec is 144.0 against a minimum_dwell_sec of 180 for LARGE_VENUE, giving a shortfall_sec of 36.0. The trace is clean — 100% coverage, 10 s cadence, no gaps, both tracks present — so the arithmetic is not in doubt.

The rider was at the pickup and actively coordinating. At 13:32:56, while the driver was inside the geofence, the rider sent 'im at the lobby, coming out'. The driver's only reply, 'ok', came at 13:33:11 — 15 seconds later — and the driver cancelled at 13:34:24, roughly 73 seconds after that reply. The rider's device track places the rider within 18.4 m of the pin throughout, well inside the 150 m rider presence radius for LARGE_VENUE, for all 45 qualifying fixes.

The driver's stated reason — 'Rider was not visible and I had another booking waiting' — is not one of the three reason codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises (RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE, EXCESSIVE_WAIT). The trip record's cancellation_reason_code is RIDER_NO_SHOW, but the driver's own contemporaneous statement shows the real motive was a competing booking, not the rider's failure to appear. Limb (d) of the baseline chargeable no-show is therefore not satisfied on the driver's own account.

The rider's message 'im at the lobby, coming out' is a locating statement — it names the rider's position at the lobby. Under POL-NS-04(a) that is exactly the kind of coordinating message the clause contemplates, and it was sent during the waiting window. The driver's reply 'ok' does not cure the shortfall: POL-NS-04(b) is about whether the driver replied within 120 seconds, but the fee's chargeability turns on the dwell under POL-NS-06, which the reply cannot extend.

The fare breakdown shows the rider was charged SGD 4.50 as a cancellation fee, with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The amount contested is SGD 4.50. Under POL-NS-06 the cancellation-fee line is refunded in full; no booking or platform fee was charged on this cancelled trip, so the full SGD 4.50 is the refund figure.

ruling.explanation:
Rider — you get the SGD 4.50 back. Driver — the fee does not stand, but not because anyone acted in bad faith.

The timeline is common ground. The trip record shows you arrived at Northpoint City at 13:31:56 and terminated the trip at 13:34:24 with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW. The GPS trace puts you inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE pickup geofence from 13:31:56 — the first qualifying in-geofence fix matches your arrival marker exactly, with speed 0.0 km/h — and you held position until 13:34:20. That is 144 seconds of continuous in-geofence dwell; the derived arrival block reports the same figures (longest_run_sec 144.0; run_count 1; shortfall_sec 36.0).

The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec; fee_schedule.defaults agrees). POL-NS-01 limb (c) requires a continuous in-geofence dwell of at least 180 seconds, measured from the first qualifying fix. 144 seconds is 36 seconds short, so limb (c) fails and the baseline charge cannot stand. Limb (d) is also short on timing: the cancellation at 13:34:24 came about 32 seconds before the 180-second dwell would have run out at 13:34:56. POL-NS-06 then applies directly: where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the free waiting period, the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded. The amount refunded is the SGD 4.50 cancellation-fee line (fare_breakdown.cancellation_fee 4.50; total_charged 4.50; payment_status CHARGED; refund_issued_sgd 0.00). No booking or platform fee was charged on this cancelled trip.

No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-06 withholds it on a shortfall, and POL-NS-07's payout engages only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full — which it is not.

On the claims. For the driver: the points that POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (b) are satisfied (arrived event present; first qualifying in-geofence fix coinciding with it) and that limb (d)'s reason code is RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three recognised codes, are accepted as facts — but the fee still fails on limb (c), and the cancellation preceded the dwell completing. The POL-NS-04 point is accepted: the driver did reply 'ok' at 13:33:11, 15 seconds after the rider's 13:32:56 message, so the rider-contact clause does not exonerate the rider; that simply leaves the case where POL-NS-06 already puts it. The description of the present state (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is accurate, but NO_ACTION is rejected as the outcome: POL-NS-06 licenses FULL_REFUND. The claim for DRIVER_COMPENSATION of SGD 3.60 (80 percent of 4.50) is rejected, because POL-NS-07 pays only on a fee that stands. The points that the arrival marker is not false (inside the radius, stationary at the arrival timestamp, so POL-NS-05 is not engaged) and that POL-NS-03 does not govern are accepted, and no false-arrival referral arises.

For the rider: the POL-NS-06 arithmetic is accepted and decides the case. The POL-NS-04 point is accepted as to the message being a locating statement ('im at the lobby, coming out'), and the rider track does place the device within about 18.4 m of the pin across all 45 fixes — but POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate because the driver replied within 120 seconds, so the refund comes from POL-NS-06, not that clause. The SGD 4.50 figure is accepted. The argument that limb (d) fails because the driver's statement ('I had another booking waiting') shows a motive other than the rider's failure to appear is rejected: POL-NS-01(d) reads the trip_record's cancellation_reason_code, which is RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three recognised codes, and the driver's separate statement is not one of that limb's tests; in any event the fee already fails on limb (c), so nothing turns on it.

Impairment and weight. Nothing the ruling rests on is impaired: the trip record, GPS trace, chat log and fare breakdown all carry weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issues, so the confidence cap is 1.0. The traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-02707-01) is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, but it is not relied on: it bears only on POL-NS-06(i), which would let separate in-geofence intervals be summed, and the trace shows a single interval (run_count 1). Two claims built on that missing artifact were discarded by the citation referee for not naming its issue code; that has no effect on the outcome.

Escalation and execution. Confidence is above the 0.70 floor, so POL-NS-09(a) is not engaged; there is no direct contradiction between admissible artifacts on arrival, dwell or rider presence (b); the parties show no repeat disputes (c); the anti-farming check does not trip (0 no-show terminations in 30 days against 54 completed trips) and the rider's no_show_disputes_30d is 1 (d); and the deciding fact is carried by unimpaired evidence (e). The SGD 4.50 refund is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold in POL-GEN-05 and executes on issue, subject to the appeal route under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
